name: orchestrator_read
description: Read one page of a resource of this ticket that the resource parameter lists. Follow next_offset, and next_resource where a page names one.

resource.description: The resource, one of: thread/<key>: one thread: its label and link, its tickets and latest decisions, and its triggers, newest first; ticket/<id>: a ticket's card, the trigger, decision and threads it is tied to, its latest assignments with the start of each report, and its inputs, newest first; ticket/<id>/assignment: its assignment text; ticket/<id>/assignments: its assignments, newest first, with the start of each report; ticket/<id>/inputs: its inputs, newest first; ticket/<id>/result: its latest report; ticket/<id>/report/<id>: the report of one of its assignments; ticket/<id>/transcript: its Executor Session's messages, newest first; ticket/<id>/message/<n>: one message of that transcript; ticket/<id>/input/<id>: one input it was delivered; trigger/<id>: a trigger's text, where it went, the message it replies to and the messages around it on its thread; prompts/<revision>: one prompt version by number, or current, the one the Session works under; feishu/<trigger-id>/…: a Feishu original, as the dsh-superagent-further-feishu skill describes; github/…: a GitHub original, as the dsh-superagent-further-github skill describes.

offset.description: Copy next_offset from the previous page; it counts characters of a text and items of a list.

limit.description: Characters of a text, 4000 by default and 8000 at most, or items of a list, 20 by default and 50 at most.

name: orchestrator_ack
description: Acknowledge one original human request before substantial work, as the replies section says; it posts as a reply to that message.

text.description: At most 100 words; Markdown is supported.

name: orchestrator_thread_unrelated
description: Stop following an attached thread that is not about this ticket, as the work section says; its own threads cannot be dropped.

thread.description: The thread key, which trigger/<id> of one of its messages shows as thread, such as feishu:<chat>:<root> or github:<number>.

reason.description: One sentence on why the thread is not about this ticket.

name: orchestrator_thread_follow
description: Follow a related thread, such as an Issue or another PR, for context only.

reason.description: How it relates, in one sentence.

name: orchestrator_trigger_handback
description: Hand back a message that asks for work beyond this ticket or for another one, for a fresh assessment; once per message. queued is false while another ticket still decides it, and for a message that was never this ticket's to decide, such as a bot's, which is assessed without it.

reason.description: One sentence on what it asks for beyond this ticket.

name: request_create
description: Raise a project request when this ticket cannot finish without a decision, a new deliverable, or work in another project of this project. The project Lead answers it; one open request per title exists for this ticket, so raising a duplicate returns it.

title.description: One line naming what the Lead must decide.

instruction.description: What is needed, in enough detail for the Lead to decide and for a worker to act on it.

kind.description: work for deliverable project work, architecture for a change of approach or its approval.

parent.description: An open project request of this project this one refines, so the Lead sees it on that request and its reply.

evidence.description: The facts that justify it, such as an error, a link, or what was tried.

name: orchestrator_report
description: Report progress, ready, blocked, failed or dropped, as the work and handoff sections say.

human_action.description: One concrete question for a person, also with state=progress; omit to keep the pending one, null to clear it.

question_for_trigger_id.description: With human_action: the human message that raised the question, which is asked where that person wrote.

pr_number.description: The ticket's PR: its source PR, or one by agent-bot from a branch named after this ticket (DSH_SUPERAGENT_NAME).

reply_to_trigger_id.description: The explicit human question this report answers; never for ordinary progress. An answer ticket's ready report already answers the question that started it.

requests.description: The project requests this ticket raised that this report answers or leaves behind; a ready, blocked, failed or dropped report must name every open one it still leaves unanswered, or the report is refused.

checks.description: The verifications this report rests on; list only checks you actually ran.

name.description: What was verified, such as "pnpm check" or "reproduced the crash".

command.description: The command that produced the evidence.

evidence.description: A short line of evidence, such as the key output or the test count.

review.description: With a review Ticket (issue #34): its verdict and the coverage statement; required by a ready report.

verdict.description: clean when the named subject met the standard, blocked when a finding does.

coverage.description: What the review actually covered, in its own words; a ready review report without it is refused.

findings.description: The concrete findings, each with its evidence.

evidence.description: What the verdict rests on, such as commands or files read.

directive_effect.description: With a person's direct Directive: what you did with it in this report — acted on it, adjusted your own work once, or handed it back as beyond your Mandate. Required by the next report after a person addressed this worker.

name: request_user_notice
description: Ask your project Lead for permission to notify the person of a fact of this Ticket (issue #29). The request is durable: the Lead approves or refuses with a reason, and only an approval sends these exact words to the person on this Ticket's channel, or the alert chat, or as attention. Never tell the person you notified them before it is approved.

text.description: The exact words the person should receive.
